A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D-MolT5 research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original 3D-MolT5 evaluations for molecular property prediction, captioning, and text-guided generation, together with ablations in Figure 3.

after.justification: V2 retains those original evaluations and adds reaction prediction, MoleculeNet evaluations, conformer analysis, and an input-fusion comparison.

M1.justification: The main E3FP tokenizer, 255M T5 architecture, embedding averaging, and pre-training objectives remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 adds a tested variant that concatenates SELFIES and E3FP tokens into one input sequence, changing fusion for that additional experiment. Algorithm 1 otherwise documents the existing tokenizer.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds USPTO-50k retrosynthesis and MoleculeNet classification on BACE, BBBP, HIV, and ClinTox. It also extends Mol-Instructions coverage beyond the previously evaluated QM9 properties to reagent prediction, forward reaction prediction, and retrosynthesis. These introduce substantially different task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds UniMoT and MolX to specialist captioning while removing the small and base MolT5 and MoMu variants. New appendix comparisons substantially broaden the comparator set, including Chemformer and ReactionT5-Large in Table 6, and GraphCL, MolCLR, GEM, and Galactica variants in Table 7.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve their dataset splits, training budgets, and metrics. Added evaluations introduce AUROC classification and an inference-only, LoRA, and full-fine-tuning breakdown for retrosynthesis. Detailed splits and training budgets for the new benchmarks are not supplied; the newly stated fourth-root task sampler is additional disclosure rather than evidence of a changed existing setting.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a five-conformer token comparison and a 3D-only prediction comparison with Uni-Mol to examine information loss from discretization. Appendix C.2 tests embedding summation against sequential concatenation, including convergence time. These substantially extend the original input/pre-training ablations; Figure 3 and the original prediction case studies are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix C and v2 Appendix F both state that reported 3D-MolT5 results are means from three independent random runs. V2 adds no confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, significance tests, or revised run-count practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and 5, retained Table 4 rows, and Figure 3 preserve their original scores. V2 adds substantial results, including 85.2 average AUROC on MoleculeNet and 0.879 forward-reaction exact match on Mol-Instructions, plus new diagnostic results and changed captioning comparator entries. These are additional evaluations, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 introduce an SE(3)-invariance argument and time/space complexity derivations, reporting O(nbk) time under a bounded-neighbor assumption and O(Nk) storage. V1 contains representation and loss definitions but no corresponding analyses. Relocating the losses and changing index conventions do not themselves change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unified discrete molecule-text modeling, E3FP-based 3D tokenization, joint pre-training, and strong performance on property prediction, captioning, and generation. V2's nearly 70% PubChemQC headline summarizes the unchanged Table 1 results; it does not establish a new performance gain or redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendices A.6 and C add substantive interpretations of discretization loss, coordinate encoding, fusion efficiency, and possible extensions to 3D generation. Appendix H explains the existing generation limitation through irreversible hashing/folding and embedding pooling. It removes the earlier limitations discussion about the small molecule-text pre-training dataset.

D1.justification: V2 adds tokenizer pseudocode, MurmurHash3 and connectivity/orientation details, a worked encoding example, special zero-embedding handling, and offline throughput information. Appendix F newly specifies fourth-root task sampling. The abstract changes a promise of forthcoming code to a stated repository link, although its availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around discrete multimodal modeling: it discusses UniMoT and MolX, introduces inspiration from Chameleon, Show-o, and Transfusion, and contrasts E3FP with direct-coordinate approaches in Appendix C.1. These additions develop relationships to alternative approaches beyond merely updating citation formatting or publication metadata.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition undergo extensive rewriting, alongside a new title and revised author/header information. Method explanations are expanded, loss definitions move from Section 3.4 to Appendix E.1, and the original appendices are reorganized around new tokenizer, evaluation, and discussion sections.

P2.justification: V2 adds Algorithm 1, encoding and conformer visualizations in Figures 4–5, and four new result tables. Figures 1–2 are restyled, and Figure 3 is redrawn with different colors, legend placement, and a vertical-axis minimum changing from 0.05 to 0.07. Existing tables are reformatted or relocated; the original case-study tables are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the tokenizer easier to inspect through pseudocode, special-case documentation, and a worked example, while adding relevant captioning comparators and targeted conformer/fusion studies. These improve explanation and supporting evidence. However, new benchmark protocols remain sparsely documented, and the new theoretical discussion overreaches: Appendix A.3 bounds shell neighbors by chemical valence despite including nonbonded atoms, while A.2 includes reflections under SE(3). These weaknesses temper the overall gains.
